rules: This round's best accept (4.142) was pure price/volume: CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($open,1)) * CS_RANK($dollar_volume). A short-horizon price delta crossed with an undifferenced dollar_volume rank is a strong class distinct from the smoothed/spread volume shapes that keep failing; don't deprioritize price/volume-only proposals.

All 6 cheap_screen failures this round were dollar_volume/volume measures resmoothed or spread against themselves or $return over windows 10-189 days (TS_COV, TS_MEAN(w1)-TS_MEAN(w2), nested TS_MEAN(TS_RANK(..)), products with TS_MEAN($return,w)). Keep a dollar_volume leg as a raw level or single rank; further smoothing or spreading it keeps failing.

TS_MIN($low,21)/($close+1e-8) is now a closed fragment: 3 rejects this round shared it verbatim (5-12 nodes) against one archived parent regardless of which fundamental ($roa/$roe/$asset_turnover) or outer structure wrapped it. Don't reuse this ratio; build the price-extension idea from a different construction.

Swapping only the fundamental leaf ($asset_turnover -> $roa or $roe) inside an already-archived CS_RANK(fundamental) * CS_RANK(price/volume payload) product is not a decorrelating edit when the payload leg is untouched; it produced 2 archive_subtree rejects this round. Change the payload leg itself, not just which profitability ratio fills the fundamental slot.

($close - TS_MIN($low,w)) / (TS_MAX($high,w) - TS_MIN($low,w)) is window-stable: the 21-day and 42-day versions correlated at rho 0.950. A window change alone will not clear correlation on this formula; change which price field anchors the numerator/denominator instead.

Ratios normalized by TS_STD($high-$low,10) collide on the denominator alone: (close-low) and (high-close) numerators over that same denominator shared 7 nodes and were rejected together. Changing only the numerator on a reused volatility-normalizer subtree is not enough; also change the window or the volatility measure.

CS_ZSCORE($operating_margin) - CS_ZSCORE(TS_RANK($dollar_volume,252)) failed coverage (0.825) even though the price side has full history; the fundamental's own sparsity is the binding constraint. When pairing any fundamental with a price/volume leg, keep that leg's window at 63 days or less.

3 of 20 proposals this round (15%) were exact duplicates of an earlier proposal in the same batch (a book_per_share/close x roe product, an eps/low-minus-return spread, a high-close-over-dollar_volume ratio). Check candidates against everything already proposed this run, not only the persistent archive.
